more_info.overview: Pectins is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include milk-based drinks and similar products intended for young children, unflavoured live fermented cream products and substitute products, both with a fat  content of less than 20 %, compote excluding products covered by category 16, jam jellies and marmalades and similar products. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Pectin is extracted with water from edible plant material, commonly citrus peel or apples. Amidated pectin is additionally treated with ammonia under alkaline conditions.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern for assessed food uses.
A human study of 36 g/day for six weeks reported no adverse effect.
